question: Where does the CLARITY market-structure bill stand, draft by draft?
answer: It is not law. The CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633) passed the House, and Senate sponsors released three public drafts: EHF26654 (616 pages, July 22, 2026), EHF26718 (630 pages, September 10, 2026) and EHF26724 (635 pages, September 14, 2026). None was formally filed as an amendment. On September 15, 2026 the Senate voted 49 to 50 on taking the bill up, short of the 60 votes needed, and the library's web check on October 19, 2026 found no later step.

items.title: Draft EHF26654
kv: The 616-page EHF26654 substitute publicly joins the Senate Banking and Agriculture market-structure products: SEC/CFTC asset and intermediary perimeters, bank authority, qualified custody, stablecoin-reward limits, software and self-custody shields, portfolio margin, a Treasury Digital Asset Cyber Innovation Center, state enforcement grants, and GENIUS lawful-order procedures for freezing, burning and reissuing stablecoins. The permanent structure legalizes private programmable rails while specifying their supervision and interruption points. Its amendment number, proposer and committee fields remain blank: public draft, not formally filed amendment, Senate-passed bill, law or running effective-date clock.

sections.title: What changed between the July 22 and September 14 drafts
sections.sub: The note's whole-text comparison, in its own words.
rows: The ethics architecture is now permanent

rows.text: **Removed:** July sections 30105 and 30106, including the January 20, 2029 sunset and the clause extinguishing liability after the sunset. **Added/rebuilt:** a `significant financial interest` test, generally an equity interest worth at least $15,000 in a business whose plurality of revenue in any of the preceding three years came from issuing or sponsoring digital assets. **Required:** divestiture or placement in a qualified blind trust by the effective date; the relevant ethics office receives notice within three days and publishes it within three days. **Penalties:** issue/sponsor violations require disgorgement plus 20 percent of consideration or $500,000, whichever is greater; significant-interest violations carry 20 percent of the interest's value or $500,000, whichever is greater; prohibited-listing violations can reach $250,000 per violation per day. **Enforcement:** the United States Attorney General receives a civil route. State attorneys general receive specified routes for injunctive relief and, for prohibited listings, civil penalties. **Drafting tension:** the intermediary prohibition in the operative text refers to assets `issued` in violation of the ban; the sponsors' one-page summary describes issued or sponsored assets. Do not silently extend the operative verb.

rows: Vertically integrated intermediaries receive an explicit control regime

rows.text: Section 20103 directs the CFTC to identify, mitigate or resolve material conflicts across registered persons, including vertically integrated structures. Common ownership or multiple registration is not banned by itself. The required controls include governance, personnel and financial-resource separation where necessary; self-dealing and unfair-pricing prohibitions; customer-asset safeguards; disclosure and management of conflicts; independent oversight; and graduated sanctions. Section 20204 generally bars a registered digital-commodity exchange and its affiliates from proprietary trading. Narrow exceptions cover customer facilitation or hedging, default management, necessary liquidity when otherwise unavailable, regulatory compliance and other CFTC-permitted transactions. Excepted trades may not be principally for profit and carry notice, reporting, information-barrier and governance requirements. Section 20206 adds conflict procedures for broker/dealer affiliate arrangements and multiple registrations.

rows: Controlled DeFi gets activity-based SEC/Treasury and CFTC routes

rows.text: Section 10301 uses control and material alterability, rather than the DeFi label alone, to distinguish a non-decentralized protocol. The analysis asks whether a person can materially alter operation outside transparent pre-established code or restrict, censor or prohibit users. Decentralized governance alone is not enough to establish control. Constrained, disclosed incident-response or security councils do not alone establish control. SEC/Treasury and CFTC rules are activity-based: securities or digital-commodity brokerage, dealing, trading, execution, clearing and custody functions are the relevant perimeter. A protocol, code or system does not itself register. A person that controls covered functions may have to register and comply with applicable BSA rules after the required rulemaking. The CFTC-side developer safe harbor is limited to cash or spot digital-commodity provisions and does not create a derivatives exemption.

rows: Stablecoin rewards now carry a deposit-flight circuit breaker

rows.text: Section 10404 still distinguishes prohibited issuer-funded interest or yield from specified rewards or benefits. New subsection 10404(c)(3)(C) defines a community bank as a depository institution or holding company with less than $10 billion in consolidated assets. If Treasury makes a written determination within 18 months after enactment that movement from interest-bearing community-bank deposits into payment stablecoins caused a substantial detrimental impact because of activities regulated by the section, Treasury must use notice-and-comment rulemaking, consult the OCC, FDIC and Federal Reserve, and prohibit comparable interest or yield by covered parties. The text places the 18-month limit on Treasury's determination. It does not plainly say that a resulting rule automatically expires after 18 months; this is a drafting question, not a resolved sunset.

rows: Federal and insured credit unions receive express parity language

rows.text: Section 10401 expressly includes federal and insured credit unions in the permission to use distributed-ledger technology or digital assets for activities otherwise authorized by law. GENIUS Act corrections add Federal Credit Union Act `accounts` to specified reserve-asset treatment and make related state-credit-union-supervisor adjustments. The provision preserves activity-specific limits. It is not a blanket authority for every derivative, brokerage, principal, dealer or market-making function.

Section 10604 now uses `blockchain developer` and `non-controlling blockchain developer or provider` terminology. The shield expressly addresses money-transmitting-business registration under 31 U.S.C. 5330, the money-transmitter definition under 31 C.F.R. 1010.100(ff)(5), and specified `financial institution` categories under 31 U.S.C. 5312. It extends the protected activity list to transaction compilation/relay/search/sequencing/validation, computational work, nodes, oracle services, bandwidth and user-controlled wallet or custody software. It removes the earlier separate express reference to 18 U.S.C. 1960 and its specific-intent transfer carveout. Other AML, sanctions and terrorism-finance law still applies to conduct outside the shield.

rows: State consumer-protection authority is preserved more expressly

rows.text: The CFTC retains exclusive jurisdiction over a registered person's covered activities. States may use the Commodity Exchange Act route against registrants, generally applicable state or local law against unregistered persons, and non-preempted unfair-or-deceptive-practice investigation and enforcement authority.

rows: A quieter AI-lab change narrows automaticity

rows.text: Section 10509 changes agency approval from `shall approve` when standards are met to `may approve`. It removes automatic approval after an additional 120-day extension. It adds a two-year project limit and a maximum of five active AI test projects per agency.

catalog_context.title: The crypto market-structure bill stalled, so the agencies moved
catalog_context.answer: The Senate failed to end debate 49–50 on September 15; the CFTC sent its own crypto rule to the White House two days later.
